verdict_reason: LiveAgent publishes a documented REST API (v1 and v3) authenticated with an API key, and its own documentation recommends using a free trial account to test the API, so credentials are self-serve. The API covers tickets, conversations, customers, companies, agents, knowledge base, files, tags and reports, giving reasonable read-write breadth. Caveats are that the complete v3 reference lives inside the logged-in account and the MCP server is listed from the Business plan.
open_questions: The full API v3 reference, scope list and permission details are only available inside a logged-in LiveAgent account and could not be verified from public pages.

Webhooks: a vendor FAQ (faq.liveagent.com/532587-How-do-I-create-a-webhook-to-receive-notifications-on-my-channel) appeared in search snippets but its page was not included in the evidence bundle, so webhook support is unverified.
Whether a dedicated sandbox/test environment exists: the vendor FAQ on sandboxes (faq.liveagent.com/839244) was not included in the bundle; the public docs only recommend a trial account for testing.
API v1 vs v3 deprecation/sunset policy is not stated in the retrieved pages.
Official SDKs: evidence only shows generating a library from the OpenAPI/Swagger descriptor; the React-library FAQ page was not in the bundle.

Which subscription plans include REST API access is unclear: MCP server is listed on Business/Enterprise, and Enterprise lists 'no plan limits' on API keys, but per-plan API key limits for lower tiers were not captured.
Whether the REST API itself supports OAuth, or OAuth 2.1 applies only to the MCP server (which also supports bearer tokens), is not explicit in the evidence.
